item.title: Beyond AI: HRM and the Work of the Future
item.content:encoded:
Sandra Fisher, FH Münster

Janet Marler, University at Albany - SUNY

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence and related technologies are transforming human resource management practices and the future of work. Building on two decades of e-HRM research, the collection seeks to understand how AI differs from previous technological advances, what new capabilities it offers for HRM, and what challenges or limitations need to be addressed. The issue welcomes both papers presented at the 10th e-HRM Conference in Muenster (June 2026) and submissions from researchers unable to attend.

The collection addresses critical questions about which HRM processes should be automated versus augmented through AI, how to mitigate concerns about bias and inequality, and how to maintain human agency and trust in AI-enabled systems. It emphasizes the role of academic research in providing evidence-based guidance on responsible AI implementation in organizations, ensuring benefits for all stakeholders including employees, managers, and organizations.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Human Resource Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • New theories and methodologies to study AI/HRM
  • New HRM strategies
  • AI-Human collaboration at work
  • e-HRM/AI value propositions
  • AI/Technology-enabled HR roles
  • AI Agents' roles and intended and unintended outcomes in HRM
  • AI/Technology-enabled HR functions: recruitment, selection, performance management, leadership, training and development, coaching, compensation and employee relations
  • Algorithmic management of employees or gig workers
  • Gig-worker management and employment/work relations
  • e-HRM and employee experience
  • e-HRM and employee wellbeing
  • AI and Bias in decision-making
  • AI and job design/crafting
  • HR data management and confidentiality
  • People Analytics and AI
  • Digital talent management
  • Employee and digital onboarding systems
  • Gamification in HRM
  • Robots and artificial intelligence (AI) in HRM
  • Employer branding and digital communication
  • AI/e-HRM and trust/ethics
